about: Why exclusive

An exclusive legal lead is an enquiry that is sent to one firm only. With Leaflegal, every lead works this way. When someone asks to speak to a solicitor about their matter, we match their enquiry to a single partner firm, send it as soon as it is checked and never pass it to anyone else, then or later.

That might sound like a small detail. In practice it changes almost everything about the first call. A client who has been introduced to one firm is expecting one call. They have time to listen, explain their situation and ask questions. A client whose details have gone to five firms gets five calls in quick succession, often from people who know nothing about them, and quickly starts to treat the whole thing as a price comparison.

People contacting a solicitor are often worried. They may be separating from a partner, facing a driving ban, chasing money their business badly needs or trying to sort out a lease before a sale falls through. A flood of calls from firms they have never heard of does not help. An exclusive introduction to one firm, which has the details of their matter in front of it, feels far more like getting help.

When you are the only firm calling, you do not need to drop everything to win a race. You still want to call quickly, because the client's need is real and their attention will not last forever. But you can use the call to understand the matter, explain how you work and talk honestly about fees. You win the work because of the service you offer, not because you happened to dial first.

Clients who feel pursued by several firms sometimes come away with a poor view of solicitors in general. An exclusive introduction treats them with more respect. It also fits more comfortably with the professional standards solicitors work to, because the conversation is about the client's needs rather than about beating competitors to the phone.

Exclusivity is only meaningful if it runs through the whole process. Our campaigns run under the Leaflegal name, so clients are not responding to adverts for several firms at once. Our forms are our own, so their details are not being collected by anyone else at the same time. And once a lead is delivered, it is never offered to another firm. Each of those steps matters. A lead that is exclusive at the moment of delivery but was collected through a shared form, or resold a week later, is not really exclusive at all.
How matching works
Every enquiry is matched to one firm using the criteria that firm has agreed with us. There is no auction and no bidding. A lead does not go to whoever is willing to pay the most on the day.

list: Practice area, such as conveyancing, family law or licensing
Matter type within that area, such as contested finances or remortgages
Location, by town, county, region or national coverage
Your monthly cap and whether you have reached it
Whether your firm is active or paused

about: If only one partner firm's criteria match an enquiry, it goes to that firm. This is common for specialist matter types and for locations where we work with a single firm.

If more than one firm could take an enquiry, we still send it to one of them. We balance distribution fairly between the firms that fit, taking account of each firm's cap and how many leads it has already received that month. No firm is starved of leads because another firm is larger.

If an enquiry does not match any partner firm's criteria, it is not forced on a firm that did not ask for it. A firm that wants only purchases in one county will not receive a remortgage from the other end of the country simply because nobody else wanted it.

Caps protect your team as well as your budget. Once you reach your monthly number, we stop matching to you until the next month. That means you are never sent more enquiries than you can call back properly, and other firms have a fair chance to receive leads that fit them.

If your firm is paused, you are left out of matching until you tell us you are ready again. Pausing is useful when a fee earner is on leave, when your team is busy with existing work or when you are moving offices. It does not affect your criteria or your agreed price, and you return to matching on the same basis as before. Leads you have already received remain yours throughout.
Never resold
Exclusivity has two parts. The first is that the enquiry goes to one firm. The second is that once it has gone to that firm, it stays there. Leaflegal never resells a delivered lead.

Once a lead reaches your firm, the client's relationship is with you. We do not send the same details to another firm a week later, add them to a list or offer them to anyone else. If the client does not instruct you, that is the end of our part in it.

Sometimes a firm cannot take on a client, perhaps because of a conflict or because the matter turns out to be outside what it does. Tell us if that happens. Your partner agreement sets out how such a lead is treated. We do not quietly pass it on to another firm without the client's knowledge.

Occasionally a client comes back to Leaflegal later with a new matter. That is a new enquiry, with its own consent, and it is matched like any other. A person who enquired about a house purchase last year might enquire about a lease extension this year, and the matching will depend on the firms whose criteria fit at that time.

We do not sell or rent personal data to anyone. Matter details are never passed to advertising platforms. This is part of how we keep exclusivity meaningful. A lead is only exclusive if the details in it are not available anywhere else.

about.h3: What this means for your records

about: Because each lead is sent once, the copy your firm receives is the only copy any law firm has from Leaflegal. Your firm becomes the controller of that copy and handles it under UK data protection law and your own privacy notice. If the client asks you about how their details reached you, the consent record that comes with every lead shows what they agreed to and when.
The first call
Exclusive leads give you room to have a proper first conversation. Firms that make the most of that room tend to follow a similar pattern.

Exclusive does not mean the client will wait forever. They asked for help because they need it, and they may look elsewhere on their own if nobody calls. Aim to call within minutes during working hours, and first thing the next morning for leads that arrive overnight.

Use the lead. Mention the type of matter, any deadline they gave and something from their own description. It tells the client straight away that you are the firm they were introduced to and that you have listened.

Tell the client they made an enquiry through Leaflegal and asked to be put in touch with a solicitor. This reassures them that the call is expected and is also a natural moment to mention the referral arrangement, which you need to make sure clients are told about.
Every Leaflegal client has said they want paid help, but most will want to know how much before they commit. Explaining your fees clearly, or when they will receive a written quote, builds trust.
End the call with something definite, such as a booked appointment, a list of documents to send or a quote to review by a certain date. Confirm it in writing the same day.

Clients do not always answer straight away. They may be at work, driving or simply wary of unknown numbers. Leave a short voicemail that mentions their enquiry, then send an email and a text with your name and direct number. Try again later the same day and the next morning. Because nobody else has been sent their details by Leaflegal, a polite, persistent approach is usually welcome rather than intrusive.
Area exclusivity
Firms sometimes ask whether they can have every Leaflegal lead for a particular town, county or matter type. This is different from lead exclusivity, which every partner firm receives.

Area exclusivity would mean no other firm receives leads that match a given location or matter type. For a firm with a strong local brand this can be attractive, because it means competitors are not receiving Leaflegal introductions in its patch.

Whether it is possible depends on the volume of enquiries in that area, how many leads the firm can realistically call back each month and the other firms we already work with. Granting one firm an area when it can only handle a fraction of the enquiries would mean clients go unhelped.
If area exclusivity matters to you, raise it on your call. We will be honest about what is realistic for your criteria. Anything agreed is written into your partner agreement.

Some firms find that what they really want is not exclusivity but focus. Narrowing your matter types to the work you most want, setting your locations around the offices you can realistically serve and choosing a cap that keeps your team busy without overloading it often achieves the same result. You receive enquiries that fit your firm closely, each one exclusive to you, without needing a special arrangement.
Every partner firm already has the most important form of exclusivity, which is that each lead it receives goes to it alone.
What it costs

Exclusive leads are priced per lead, at a price agreed with your firm before you start. We do not publish prices, because the value of a lead varies a great deal between practice areas, matter types and locations.

An exclusive lead usually costs more than a shared one. The useful comparison is not the price of a lead but the cost of winning an instruction. If a shared lead goes to several firms and only one can win it, each firm is paying for a fraction of a chance. With an exclusive lead, the whole chance is yours.

Exclusive leads also save time that is easy to overlook. With shared leads, intake staff spend a large part of their day calling people who have already been contacted by other firms, explaining who they are and competing on price. With exclusive leads that time goes into conversations about the client's matter. For a busy team, that difference can matter as much as the price of the lead itself.

The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that you set a monthly cap and can change it or pause at any time. Pricing, billing, volumes, delivery and the rules for invalid leads are set out in your partner agreement before your first lead.
Leaflegal does not charge clients anything. We tell them that we are paid by the firms we introduce them to.
To find out what exclusive leads would cost for your firm, apply to become a partner firm and book a 30-minute call. We will show you a sample lead and put a proposal together.
faqs: Exclusivity explained
What does exclusive mean for a Leaflegal lead?

It means the enquiry is sent to your firm and no other. We do not send the same lead to several firms at once, and we never resell a lead after it has been delivered. When you call the client, you are the only firm Leaflegal has introduced them to for that matter.
Are your leads ever resold?

No. Once a lead is delivered to your firm, it stays with your firm. We do not pass it to another firm later, add it to a list or sell the details to anyone. We do not sell or rent personal data at all. Your copy of a lead is the only copy any law firm receives from us.
Can the client still talk to other firms?

Yes. Exclusive describes what Leaflegal does, not what the client does. Some clients will look at other firms on their own, especially for higher value matters. Calling quickly, listening carefully and being clear about fees gives you the best chance of being the firm they choose. A prompt, useful first call usually counts for a lot.
How is an exclusive lead different from a shared lead?

A shared lead is sent to several firms, so the client receives several calls and the first firm to reach them usually wins. An exclusive lead goes to one firm, so the first call can focus on the client's matter rather than on beating competitors to the phone. It also tends to feel calmer for the client.
Is exclusivity guaranteed in writing?

The way leads are delivered and handled is set out in your partner agreement, which you see and agree before your first lead. If you have specific questions about exclusivity, raise them on your call and we will explain how it applies to your criteria. Exclusivity is not an extra you pay for or an option some firms receive. It is how every Leaflegal lead is handled, for every partner firm.
Why don't more lead sellers offer exclusive leads?

Selling each lead several times brings in more money per enquiry, so shared leads are attractive to sellers. Exclusive leads cost more to produce, because every enquiry can only be sold once. We think the better experience for clients and firms is worth it. It also suits the way most solicitors prefer to work, with a proper conversation rather than a race.
Are your adverts shared with other lead sellers?

No. Our campaigns run under the Leaflegal name and lead to our own enquiry forms. We do not collect enquiries on behalf of other lead sellers or take enquiries from them. That is part of what makes each lead genuinely exclusive, because the client's details are not being gathered by several companies at the same time.
Matching and fairness
How do you decide which firm receives a lead?

Each lead goes to a firm whose practice areas, matter types and locations it fits, taking account of each firm's monthly cap and whether the firm is paused. Where more than one firm fits, we balance distribution fairly between them. Your criteria and cap are agreed with you in advance, so you always know what kind of enquiries can come your way.
Is there an auction or bidding?

No. Leads are not sold to the highest bidder on the day. Each firm has an agreed price and agreed criteria, and leads are matched against those. This keeps things predictable for firms and stops costs rising without warning. Your price is set out in your partner agreement and only changes if you and we agree a change.
Will a larger firm get all the leads?

No. Where several firms fit an enquiry, we balance distribution fairly, taking account of each firm's cap and how many leads it has already received that month. A smaller firm with a lower cap still receives its fair share of matching enquiries. Distribution is about fit and fairness, not about the size of the firm or how many leads it asked for.
What happens when I reach my monthly cap?

We stop matching to your firm until the next month. Enquiries that would have gone to you can be matched to other firms whose criteria fit. If you want more, you can raise your cap at any time by telling our team. Your cap also sets the most you will spend on leads that month.
What if my criteria overlap with another firm's?

That is common, especially in larger towns and cities. Both firms remain eligible for enquiries that fit, and each lead still goes to only one of them. Fair distribution means neither firm is consistently overlooked. Narrowing your matter types or locations to the work you most want can make your matching more focused, but overlap is normal and nothing to worry about.
Can I see which other firms are in my area?

We do not share the details of other partner firms. What we can do is give you an honest view of the likely volume of leads for your criteria and explain how distribution works where several firms fit. We treat every partner firm's details as confidential, in the same way we treat yours. Other firms do not see your criteria, volume or price either.
Do you ever send a lead outside my criteria?

We aim not to. Each lead is matched against your practice areas, matter types and locations. If a lead clearly falls outside the criteria agreed with you, it may count as invalid under your partner agreement. Tell us within the review period, and we will also look at why it happened so it does not happen again.
Area exclusivity
Can I have exclusivity over a whole town?

Possibly. It depends on the volume of enquiries in that town, how many leads your firm can call back each month and the other firms we work with. Raise it on your call and we will be honest about whether it is realistic. Anything agreed is written into your partner agreement.
Can I have exclusivity over a matter type?

The same considerations apply. If you are the only firm that wants a particular matter type in your area, you may be the only one receiving it anyway. If several firms want it, exclusivity would need to make sense for clients as well as for you. Raise it on your call.
Does area exclusivity cost more?

If it is available, it would be reflected in your proposal. Pricing depends on practice area, matter type, location and volume, and any special arrangement is agreed with you before you start. We will explain any difference clearly. Any arrangement would be set out in your proposal and written into your partner agreement before it applied, so there would be no surprises.
What if I cannot handle all the leads in my area?

Then area exclusivity would probably not suit you, because clients would go unhelped. A monthly cap that matches your team's capacity is a better approach. You still receive every lead on an exclusive basis. A cap set at the number your team can call back quickly protects both your budget and the clients who enquire. You can raise it once your team has more capacity.
Can area exclusivity be reviewed later?

If an arrangement is agreed, how and when it is reviewed would be set out in your partner agreement. Volumes change over time, as do the needs of your firm. We would rather revisit an arrangement than leave clients waiting because a firm has more leads than it can handle.
When things change
What if I cannot act for a client?

Tell us. It might be a conflict, a matter outside your expertise or a client you are unable to help for another reason. Your partner agreement sets out how such a lead is treated. We never quietly pass a lead to another firm without the client's knowledge. Clients should not be left waiting.
What if a client enquires again later?

A new enquiry about a new matter is a new lead with its own consent. It is matched against the criteria of partner firms at that time, in the same way as any other enquiry. It might come to you, or to another firm whose criteria fit better. The new enquiry has its own consent record.
Can I pause and keep my exclusivity?

You can pause at any time. While you are paused, enquiries that would have matched you can be matched to other firms. Every lead you receive when you return is still exclusive to you. Pausing does not affect your criteria or your agreed price. When you are ready again, tell our team and we will start matching to your firm straight away.
What if I change my criteria?

Tell our team and we will update your matching. Your new criteria apply to enquiries that arrive after the change. Leads already delivered to you remain yours. You can add or remove matter types, widen or narrow your locations and raise or lower your cap whenever your firm's needs change.
What if the client has already instructed another firm?

This occasionally happens, because clients can look elsewhere on their own. If they instructed another firm after enquiring with us, the lead is still valid, in the same way as when a client chooses not to proceed. Calling quickly is the best way to make sure you are the first solicitor they speak to.
Cost and value
Do exclusive leads cost more?

Usually, yes, compared with shared leads, because each enquiry can only be sold once. Pricing depends on the practice area, matter type, location and volume, and is agreed with your firm before you start. We will put a proposal together after your call. The difference is that you are paying for the whole chance to win the work rather than a share of it.
How should I compare exclusive and shared leads?

Compare the cost of winning an instruction rather than the price of a lead. Count the time spent calling people who have already spoken to other firms, and the fees lost to price competition. Many firms find exclusive leads compare well once those costs are included. Your own records give the fairest answer.
Is there a minimum?

Yes. The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that you set a monthly cap, which you can change or pause at any time. Ten a month is enough to judge the quality of exclusive leads and see how they fit with your team. Many firms start near the minimum and increase their cap once they are comfortable.
Do clients pay for the introduction?

No. Leaflegal does not charge clients anything. Your firm pays for the introduction, and the client agrees fees directly with you. Clients are told that Leaflegal is paid by the firms it introduces them to. Our arrangement with your firm does not change what the client pays you. You agree your fees with the client in the usual way, and the client is free to decide whether to instruct you.
How do I find out what exclusive leads would cost me?

Apply to become a partner firm and book a 30-minute call. We will talk about your practice areas, matter types, locations and volume, show you a sample lead and then send you a proposal with your price per lead. There is no obligation to go ahead after the call. You can take time to look at the proposal and ask questions before deciding.
Can I measure the return on exclusive leads?

Yes. Because each lead has an agreed price, you can compare what you spend in a month with the instructions and fees that leads bring in. Keep a simple record of each lead and its outcome, by practice area. Sharing what you find with us also helps us refine your criteria towards the work you want most.
